title: The Turtles That Remember
text:
A green turtle hatches at night, no bigger than the palm of your hand, and scrambles down the sand towards the sound of the waves. Most of them never make it. Crabs, birds and fish are waiting.
The few that survive disappear into the open ocean for decades. They cross thousands of kilometres of water, feeding in seagrass beds far from where they began, growing slowly in a world with no landmarks at all.
And then, after twenty or thirty years, something extraordinary happens. The females turn around and swim back — not to any convenient beach, but to the exact stretch of sand where they hatched.
Scientists believe they read the magnetic field of the Earth itself, carrying a memory of one beach for half a lifetime. What is certain is this: if that beach is built over, there is nowhere else they will go.
